neighbours.label: A classifying modifier naming a scholarly method or lens, in the slot before 'analysis / approach / perspective / method / imaging' ('social network analysis', 'a systems approach', 'an institutional perspective'); the same words in everyday noun phrases stay quiet
fire: The second chapter applies an institutional perspective to the history of central banks.
Sociologists relied on social network analysis to trace how the rumour spread.
The engineers adopted a systems approach to the problem of urban flooding.
Neurologists used functional imaging to compare the two groups of patients.
Linguists applied the comparative method to reconstruct the lost parent language.
The report takes an institutional approach to explaining why reforms stall.
Biologists turned to network analysis to study how the proteins interact.
The course teaches a systems perspective on managing hospital waiting lists.
quiet: The second chapter describes the grey institutional corridors of the old hospital.
Sociologists complained that the office network was slow all morning.
The engineers restarted both systems after the power cut.
Neurologists agreed that the old scanner was barely functional by then.
Linguists found the rent comparatively cheap in the lost mountain village.
The report was printed on thick paper and bound in blue cloth.
Biologists hung a fine net over the pond to keep the herons out.
The course ends with a picnic on the hospital lawn.
